Course Schedule

Milestones are due Sunday 11:59 PM PT. Standups (~10 min) open every session from S5. Paper presentations (two or three pairs) open S13–S18.

S Wk Date Day Topic Reading Due
Act I: Structure
S1 1 Mar 29 M What architecture is: structures, views, decisions. The system we inherit: platform tour, contracts, team assignments. ICA: sketch one inherited service's box-and-line diagram from its repo B Ch. 1–2; CT What Architecture Is; Perry & Wolf (1992)
S2 1 Mar 31 W Components, connectors, configurations; prescriptive vs. descriptive architecture; drift and erosion; recovery methods. ICA: name every connector on the platform's request path CT Components, Connectors, and Configurations; CT Architecture Recovery; Mehta et al. (2000) Survey
S3 2 Apr 5 M Styles within one process: layers, pipes and filters, repository and blackboard, microkernel and plug-in, the MVC family CT Styles Within One Process; Shaw & Clements (1997)
S4 2 Apr 7 W Styles across processes: client-server, broker, publish-subscribe, service-based, microservices, peer-to-peer; scale-independence. Decisions and ADRs. ICA: reconstruct an inherited ADR CT Styles Across Processes; CT Architecture Decisions and ADRs; Nygard (2011) G0 (Sun Apr 11)
Act II: Qualities
S5 3 Apr 12 M Quality attributes: six-part scenarios, utility trees, ISO/IEC 25010. ICA: turn inherited-evaluation risks into scenarios B Ch. 3, 14; CT Quality-Attribute Scenarios and Utility Trees; Barbacci et al. (2002)
S6 3 Apr 14 W Availability and performance tactics and patterns: redundancy, circuit breakers, caching, queues, concurrency B Ch. 4, 9; CT Tactics for Runtime Qualities Paper sign-up
S7 4 Apr 19 M Modifiability, integrability, testability: coupling and cohesion, information hiding, intermediaries, test seams B Ch. 7, 8, 12; CT Tactics for Change; Parnas (1972)
S8 4 Apr 21 W Security, deployability, safety, energy: tactics survey; pipelines, canary and blue-green releases, feature flags B Ch. 5, 6, 10, 11 H1 usability scenarios arrive from CSS 478 (Wed); G1 (Sun Apr 25)
S9 5 Apr 26 M Usability as architecture: undo, cancel, progress, user models; reading a UX team's scenarios as ASRs; accessibility as a quality B Ch. 13; CT Usability-Supporting Architecture; Bass, John & Kates (2001)
S10 5 Apr 28 W Midterm (Sessions 1–8, 90 min)
Act III: Method
S11 6 May 3 M Architecturally significant requirements; Attribute-Driven Design, worked on one inherited service; evolving a running system: strangler fig, branch by abstraction, parallel run, modular monolith B Ch. 19–20; CT ASRs and Attribute-Driven Design; CT Evolving a Running System; Fowler (2004)
S12 6 May 5 W Describing architecture: views and viewpoints, 4+1, C4, ADLs, ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010. ICA: check a G2 draft against a viewpoint B Ch. 22; CT Describing Architecture; Kruchten (1995) H2 prototypes arrive (Wed); G2 (Sun May 9)
Act IV: Distribution and AI Components
S13 7 May 10 M REST and interfaces: Fielding's constraints and the properties each induces, Richardson maturity levels; REST, gRPC, GraphQL, events; contracts, versioning, compatibility B Ch. 15; CT REST as a Derived Style; CT Interfaces and Integration; Fielding et al. (2017)
S14 7 May 12 W ML- and LLM-enabled systems: the model as a component (nondeterminism, drift), data and model pipelines, integrating foundation models (prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, fine-tuning, agents and tool use), guardrails, cost and latency budgets, monitoring. ICA: write scenarios for an AI feature of the course system EAI Ch. 4 (Foundation Models) and the AI model life-cycle chapter; CT ML- and LLM-Enabled Systems; Sculley et al. (2015) G3 (Sun May 16)
S15 8 May 17 M Distributed data: replication, consistency models, CAP and PACELC, sagas, event sourcing, CQRS CT Distributed Data; Brewer (2012); DeCandia et al. (2007)
S16 8 May 19 W Microservices and platforms: decomposition by bounded context, data ownership, Conway's law; containers, orchestration, observability B Ch. 16–17; CT Microservices; CT Platforms; Conway (1968) H4 test findings arrive (Sun May 23)
Act V: Evolution
S17 9 May 24 M Lightweight evaluation and conformance: mini-ATAM, design reviews, fitness functions as conformance checks. ICA: peer evaluation of G3 increments (CSS 555 alumni lead) B Ch. 21; CT Lightweight Evaluation; Kazman et al. (1998)
S18 9 May 26 W Architecture debt and the laws of software evolution; product lines, platforms, and domain-specific architectures; the architect in the organization, team structure B Ch. 23–25; CT Architecture Debt; CT Product Lines; Lehman (1980); Bosch (2009)
10 May 31 M Memorial Day: no class
S19 10 Jun 2 W G4 presentations (15 min per team); course wrap-up G4 package (Sun Jun 6)
11 Jun 7–11 Final exam (date and time per UW finals schedule) Final exam
